section.sectionSummaryBrief: After all this, at the Giving of the Torah there was only a beginning, and the actual fulfillment and acceptance occurred specifically during the time of exile, especially in Haman's time when Israel was at the lowest point.
section.t: And after all this,
behold, at the Giving of the Torah there was only "they began to do,"
a matter of a beginning only,
and the fulfillment
(of the Torah of the Giving of the Torah),
"they fulfilled and accepted,"
was specifically in the time of exile,
and particularly in the time of Haman when Israel were at the ultimate low of exile in physicality and spirituality,
which is a most wondrous matter.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This is understood through the explanation of "pure pressed oil for illumination," that when a person is in a state of being crushed and broken, he reaches the light source itself, even if he is in a state of great physical expansion or even spiritual perfection, through contemplating the greatness of Hashem and his own lowliness.
section.t: And this will be understood
(as explained in the maamar20)
according to the explanation of the verse21
"pure pressed oil for illumination,"
where it is precisely noted22
that it does not say "oil to give light" but rather "oil for illumination,"
and he explains regarding this23
that "illumination" refers to the light source itself,
meaning the source of light.
And this is what is said, "pure pressed for illumination,"
that when a person is in a state of being crushed,
broken and crushed,
behold, then he reaches the light source.
And this being broken and crushed is also when physically he is in a state of the greatest expansion, yet nevertheless he lacks in spirituality,
in his service,
and moreover,
that even if also in spirituality he is perfect in fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos,
and even to the point that he is at the ultimate level and expansion, serving his service as is proper for him to do24,
nevertheless, when he contemplates that "and Your people are all righteous"25,
and each and every Jew is "a planting of My planting, the work of My hands in which to take pride"
(the plantings and the works of the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He, and in them He takes pride),
and he contemplates the greatness of the Holy One, blessed be He,
behold, he will weep bitterly in his soul,
for what is all his service considered
(even if it is perfect)

relative to his true value and level that he must be a planting of His planting and the work of His hands for the pride of the Holy One, blessed be He, in a revealed way, so that all who see him will recognize this,
and if so, even the perfection of his service is not at all as it should be,
and behold, even one who strikes with a hammer before the king, this is the opposite of life and existence26,
and all the more so when his service is not as it should be,
that it is not commensurate with what should have been according to the powers given to him.
And behold, when he contemplates the greatness of his descent and weeps bitterly in his soul,
he will come to repentance,
and even to the point of reaching "and the spirit returns to God who gave it"27
and even higher,
that the soul returns with self-sacrifice to its source and supernal root from which it was taken, etc.28.
And this is what is said, "pure pressed for illumination,"
that through this, that a person is broken and crushed,
in a state of being crushed
[from within expansion in physicality and from within expansion in spirituality,
as above],
behold, then he reaches the light source itself,
to the level of "the God who gave it," etc.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This work of being in ultimate self-nullification in a state of being crushed then also affects actual practice, enabling one to serve with complete perfection through all changes and seasons without any extraneous thought.
section.t: And behold, the aforementioned service of being in ultimate self-nullification in a state of being crushed then also affects actual practice.
And the matter is,
as the Alter Rebbe explains in Torah Or29
that the Jews gave themselves over to death all year long and no extraneous thought arose in them, G-d forbid,
that the explanation of this is that they stood with self-sacrifice in all manners of changes that occurred,
for this is "shanah" (year), a term of change30
because the year includes within it all possible changes31.
And in the known manner32
regarding the virtue of the esrog, which dwells on its tree from year to year33
that it bears upon itself all the changes of the airs of the four seasons of the year and is not affected by this at all, and dwells on its tree
[that its vitality and place of dwelling is on its tree,
in its root and source],
and not only is it not affected by the changes, but moreover it grows from the changes,
as explained in the continuation "and so"34,
behold, in this manner is the service of man,
that in all manners of changes of levels in service,
the entire year,
his service is in ultimate perfection,
that no extraneous thought arises, G-d forbid.
And one reaches this specifically when he is in ultimate self-nullification in a state of being crushed,
because since there are different modes of service from one extreme to the other, like kindness and severity,
therefore even if his service in the line of kindness is as it should be, it might be difficult for him that his service in the line of severity should also be with that same perfection
[in the manner that even regarding Avraham Avinu,
since his service was in the aspect of kindness35,
"Avraham who loves Me"36,
it is said of him37
"Now I know that you are a G-d-fearing man,"
after he also stood in the tenth trial38],
and through the self-nullification of being crushed, the perfection of his service is without changes in all the different modes of service39.
